messages.subject: [rkward-users] Upcoming release 0.6.4 - Call for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

We are getting ready to release RKWard 0.6.4 to the public, and as
usual, I would like to ask your help in finding the last few rough
edges that we should take care of.

Once again, we'll try to make do with a rather short testing period,
and so I'd like to ask you to provide feedback by December 14 (the
earlier the better). Naturally, if anything important comes up, the
testing period will be extended as necessary. More details and download
links at https://rkward.kde.org/Release_Schedule .

Key new features to look out for, are:
- The integrated HTML window (also used for the "Output Window") has
  been changed to be based on the Qt webkit engine. This is partly in
  preparation for the port to "KDE 5", but should hopefully also
  address some issues with drag-and-drop of images or text from the
  output window to e.g. a word processor.
- With the help of usability expert Jan Dittrich, we addressed some of
  the more important points of confusion: The "Worksapce browser" has
  been re-designed (and also gained search-functionality), the
  "optionset" element used in some plugins has been reworked to be much
  more intuitive, but also the CVS import plugin has seen further
  improvements in usability, and many small problems have been fixed
  across the board. 

--- Translators ---

As a last reminder: We are hosted on KDE.org since version 0.6.3, and
translations are managed, there. Your existing translations files
should have been imported. If you have not done so, yet, get in touch
with your KDE language team (http://l10n.kde.org/teams-list.php).

This also means that calls for translations are no longer sent to this
list! https://mail.kde.org/mailman/listinfo/kde-i18n-doc is the list
for this, now.

Thanks!
Thomas

messages.subject: Small changes to mailing lists
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

We recently started being affected by the problem that the "DMARC"
policy of Yahoo (and some other providers) breaks traditional mailing
list setups. Most subscribers on rkward-devel and rkward-users will not
have noticed anything, some will have been missing out on certain
mails, and - worse - have had their subscription suspended,
automatically, due to their mail providers rejecting too many mails from
the list.

Apologies for that. I have re-enabled your subscriptions, and I have
made the following changes to the mailing lists, hoping these will be
enough to keep the problem from happening in the future:

- Mailing list mails are no longer prefixed with [rkward-devel] or
  [rkward-users]. If you were basing filtering rules on this, please
  switch to using the "List-ID" header field, instead.
- The Reply-To:-address is no longer explicitly pointed to the mailing
  list. Whether or not this changes anything for you, depends on your
  email / webmail software. When replying to mailing list posts, please
  do give the "To:"-field a quick glance. In most cases it is
  appropriate to direct your replies to the mailing list (other people
  will be interested in seeing your answers / follow-ups, too). If in
  doubt, use the "Reply to all" function of your email software.
- Mailing list mails no longer contain a footer message with links to
  the list info pages. For reference, these are
  https://mail.kde.org/mailman/listinfo/rkward-devel and
  https://mail.kde.org/mailman/listinfo/rkward-users , respectively.

Background info: http://wiki.list.org/DEV/DMARC .

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: How to change RKWard's search path to R backend
messages.subject_clean: How to change RKWard's search path to R backend
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've looked all over the internet for an answer to the Subject query 
without success.  Hopefully, you experts can set me straight.

I'm running ubuntu 14.04 32 bit machine with ARKward 0.6.1 version. When 
I invoke RKWard it searches and finds R version 3.0.2 installed at 
/usr/bin.  This is an old version of the backend.  I have a 3.2.2 R 
version installed at /usr/local/bin.  It functions superbly in console mode.

How can I set RKWard's search path so that it finds the version at 
/usr/local/bin?

Thanks,
Mark Allyn

messages.subject: How to change RKWard's search path to R backend
messages.subject_clean: How to change RKWard's search path to R backend
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Sun, 13 Dec 2015 11:09:20 -0500
mark allyn <mark.allyn at verizon.net> wrote:
> I've looked all over the internet for an answer to the Subject query 
> without success.  Hopefully, you experts can set me straight.
> 
> I'm running ubuntu 14.04 32 bit machine with ARKward 0.6.1 version.
> When I invoke RKWard it searches and finds R version 3.0.2 installed
> at /usr/bin.  This is an old version of the backend.  I have a 3.2.2
> R version installed at /usr/local/bin.  It functions superbly in
> console mode.
> 
> How can I set RKWard's search path so that it finds the version at 
> /usr/local/bin?

Several parts to this answer:
1. RKWard 0.6.1 is pretty old. 0.6.3 is current, 0.6.4 to be released
soon. We provide backports for various Ubuntu series at
https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel .
2. Starting with RKWard version 0.6.2, there is a command-line option
--r-executable to change the R version to be used at runtime. However,
3. RKWard _should_ be compiled against the version of R you want to be
using, and _must_ install some files into the library location of that
version of R. Neither is the case on your installation. Therefore, what
you are trying to achieve will not work, this way. You can either:
4. Compile and install RKWard from source, as I described on
rkward-devel, the other day. Be sure to specify the correct R
installation in the cmake command line, of course. If you want to keep
the version of R in /usr/local/bin/R, this is the way to go for you.
5. Alternatively, again, use one of our "CRAN version of R"-PPAs. This
will give you an RKWard compiled for a recent version of R, *with R
installed in /usr/bin/R*

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: rkwarddev 0.08-1 released
messages.body_plain:
hi,

in preparation of the forthcoming RKWard release, here's rkwarddev 0.08-1:
 https://files.kde.org/rkward/R/pckg/rkwarddev/index.html

you can find the comprehensive ChangeLog here:
 https://files.kde.org/rkward/R/pckg/rkwarddev/NEWS.html

amongst a lot of fixes and minor improvements, there are some major steps 
forward in this release:

 - JavaScript code generation is much more straight forward with the new js() 
   wrapper. it preserves "if(...){...}else{...}" conditions as well as common 
   operators like "==", ">" or "!", making your code easier to read/compare

 - existing plugin XML code can be translated into rkwarddev code (and its
   validity checked) by the new method plugin2script()

 - there are new getter/setter functions to define output characteristics, 
   like the character used for indentation globally just once

if you are interested in RKWard plugin development, check it out!


viele grüße :: m.eik
